intent: Give composition-only meta-workflows a bounded live node catalogue and a check-only gate for AI-drafted workflow specs.

example.input: A request for a simple text notification; then an aotn-workflow/1 JSON draft using registered nodes.
example.expected_result: Relevant real contracts fit the context budget. A valid draft continues as the parsed spec; an invalid draft takes the error path with node/field/message problems. Neither node saves or executes a workflow.

target_device: Owner WSL terminal, 80x24 and wider; future AI steps consume the data.
trigger: On demand inside a future composition-only meta-workflow; no schedule or live activation.
inputs: Current NodeFactory registry and static metadata
JSON text in aotn-workflow/1 from an upstream answer, Vault or configured long-text field
constraints: Steps 0–4 only; decisions and samples need owner approval before any build
No product code, generated node files, PR, workflow-library saves or execution
Functionality and AI-runnability before UI polish; use real styles.tcss
Reuse the same checks as aotn build --check; do not invent a second validator
Exclude internal/tombstone types; expose uncertainty and size failures
No network, model generation, spending, account setup or live settings changes
success: Catalogue has type/display name/description/group, typed inputs/outputs/sources, key config and declared errors
All/filter and compact/detailed are independent of Text/JSON output choices
The size limit never cuts JSON or silently removes required contract fields
Valid output is the parsed input spec, preserving handles/config, not a saved workflow or generated ids
Invalid errors have readable bounded problem rows with node, field and message
The future approval/build gaps are explicit and not treated as authorized work
unknowns: Owner decisions 1–12 and approval of these exact samples remain pending
Final cap/filter ergonomics and current-registry all-node output sizes need build verification
No new node has been implemented or run; no independent review or real-device proof
